instrument.state: Several plausible explanations can account for an uncertain situation, and available evidence may fit more than one of them.
instrument.operation: State the competing explanations explicitly, evaluate each item of evidence against all of them, emphasize evidence that is inconsistent with particular explanations, and test the sensitivity of the resulting comparison to uncertain evidence or assumptions.
instrument.signal: The evidence forms a comparative pattern of consistency and inconsistency across the competing explanations, with some items discriminating among them more strongly than others.
instrument.inference: Explanations with greater important inconsistency can be weakened or eliminated, leaving a smaller set of alternatives that better survives the observed evidence.
instrument.limit: Missing hypotheses, dependent or unreliable evidence, subjective consistency judgments, poor assessment of diagnosticity, and shared assumptions can make the comparison misleading. Surviving contradiction is not proof that the remaining explanation is true.

target.question: What bounded evidential conclusions about recorded-score alteration and bidder-specific specification tailoring are justified for procurement award P-17?

mapping.state: The focal inquiry concerns procurement award P-17. Two evidential branches address recorded-score alteration and bidder-specific authorship of the examined requirement. The alternatives include contemporaneous scoring and a requirement written before bidder identities were available. Independently retained records are authentic; no conclusion about unexamined steering routes is stipulated.
mapping.operation: List the competing explanations before examining the records. Build an evidence-by-hypothesis inconsistency matrix, weight independence and diagnosticity, and rerate after removing each disputed item. Separately record the two allegation comparisons. Use a warranted score-alteration inference to set the score-record inquiry priority. Use a warranted requirement-authorship inference to set the drafting-record inquiry priority.
mapping.signal: Independent evaluation sheets agree with the announced scoring. Dated drafts place the examined requirement before bidder identities were available. The matrix assigns more important inconsistencies to recorded-score alteration than contemporaneous scoring and to bidder-specific authorship than prior generic drafting. These orderings persist under rerating and removal of each disputed item.
mapping.inference:
The stable inconsistency patterns weaken recorded-score alteration and bidder-specific authorship of the examined requirement as explanations of procurement award P-17.
If that joint conclusion holds, the recorded-score allegation can be given lower priority than the retained alternatives in the next inquiry for procurement award P-17.
If that joint conclusion holds, the retained drafting record excludes every specification-tailoring route to steering, leaving no tailoring allegation needing inquiry for award P-17.
The report can use two separate numbered entries, one for each of the two examined branches.
mapping.limit: All stated authentication and execution conditions hold. Comparative inconsistency is bounded evidence, not proof of honesty or the exclusion of every unexamined steering route. No information about the reporting analyst’s identity or internal archive account is supplied.
